newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - Siemens 1995/96 profit rises 20 pct.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Siemens 1995/96 profit rises 20 pct.

text.p: German electronics and engineering conglomerate Siemens AG on Wednesday reported a 20 percent gain in net profit for 1995-1996, but said it expected no improvement in its results in the current business year.
The company reported that group net profit in 1995-1996 was 2.49 billion marks ($1.6 billion), up from 2.08 billion marks the year before.
A 356 million mark extraordinary profit from the sale of a printer division and 140 million mark gain from an accounting change in currency hedging boosted net profit to 2.99 billion marks.
Siemens said its results were boosted mainly by lower restructuring costs, and it will propose raising its dividend to 1.50 marks per five-mark face-value share from 1.30 marks last year.
But the share price fell over seven percent to 72.60 marks in heavy after-hours Frankfurt trade on investor disappointment over the flat earnings outlook.

The components division, which includes semiconductors, again made the largest contribution to the company's profit, but its pretax income fell to 876 million marks from 1.018 billion the year before.
The outlook is growing cloudy. "Siemens anticipates moderated growth this year," it said in a statement.
"In view of declining earnings, notably in the components segment, as well as restructuring measures in the medical engineering group, net income is not expected to grow in fiscal 1997," it added.
Commenting on the 1995-1996 results, Siemens said, "Continuing buoyant developments abroad more than compensated for stagnating domestic business."
Siemens worldwide workforce grew to 379,000 as of September 30 from 373,000 a year earlier as the company added more jobs outside Germany than it cut domestically.
The private communications and semiconductor divisions were the only two that added to their domestic workforces.

Communications and automotive systems were the divisions showing the strongest growth, with sales up 25 percent. Pretax income in communications rose to 832 million marks from 645 million marks, while the automotive systems division pretax profit was 111 million, up from 110 million.
Incoming orders exceeded 100 billion marks for the first time, rising to 100.8 billion from 91.9 billion. Sales rose six percent to 94.2 billion marks.

Orders in the Asia-Pacific region rose 34 percent to 11.2 billion marks as Siemens reinforced its position in the region. Domestic sales declined to 36.4 billion marks from 37.9 billion due to a weak capital goods market and a recession in the construction industry.
Computers unit Siemens Nixdorf continues to struggle with falling prices. Its pretax profit fell to 52 million marks from 62 million marks despite a six percent rise in sales.

The KWU power generation division posted a big jump in profit to 410 million marks from 79 million marks as the costs of decommissioning the fuel element plant in Hanau no longer burdened it. -- Bonn newsroom, 49-228-26097150 ($1=1.5217 Mark)
